summary: Iteration 7 — Retest of MSG91 OTP phone-normalization bug fix (spec #5). RESULT: FIX VERIFIED, FULL REGRESSION GREEN. Ran /app/backend/tests/test_msg91_otp_iter6.py → 21/21 pass (previously 20/21 — the sole failing test `TestDevPhoneNormalization::test_all_three_formats_resolve_to_same_user` now PASSES). Full suite (backend_test + test_referrals_favorites_tips + test_security_iter3 + test_admin_iter4 + test_msg91_otp_iter6) → 99/99 pass in 110s after a 1-line test assertion update in test_admin_iter4.py::test_admin_complaints_list_and_resolve (the test asserted raw 10-digit phone equality; now correctly asserts canonical `91XXXXXXXXXX` shape — the assertion needed to catch up with the intentional storage-format change). All 4 spec requirements manually verified via live preview URL: (1) `+919825083028`, `9825083028`, `91-9825-083-028` all resolve to SAME user id (verified by 3 separate verify-otp calls returning identical `user.id`); (2) stored user.phone is `919825083028` — confirmed via `GET /api/auth/me`; (3) referral_code = `ZIP3028XX` uses canonical last-4 digits (matches DB `phone[-4:]`, not raw input's last-4 which would collide across formats); (4) admin path (phone=9999999999, role=admin) still logs in with OTP 1234 and stores phone as raw `9999999999` (NOT `919999999999`) — admin bypass preserved. Code review of the fix at /app/backend/server.py L344-418 is clean: (a) admin branch unchanged, canonical_phone = ADMIN_PHONE (raw); (b) non-admin branch always calls normalize_indian_phone(payload.phone) BEFORE the MSG91/DB path, so invalid phones now 400 in BOTH dev AND prod (bonus fix for previous iter6 minor issue #4 — dev-mode verify-otp now validates phone shape); (c) canonical_phone is the single source of truth for find_one query filter, update_one filter, insert doc `phone` field, and referral_code `phone[-4:]` — no drift. Note per request: pre-fix users with raw-phone rows are unreachable via canonical lookup and will create new rows on next login — this is expected/acceptable dev behaviour and not tested against. No frontend testing performed (backend-only per request).

minor.issue: test_admin_iter4.py::test_admin_complaints_list_and_resolve had a hardcoded assertion `target['user']['phone'] == phone` (raw 10-digit) that broke after the canonical-storage fix. Updated to `== f'91{phone}'`. Other tests in test_admin_iter4 already used `customer['user']['phone']` (looked up from server response) so they were unaffected.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix at server.py L344-418 correctly channels ALL non-admin phone usage through canonical_phone = normalize_indian_phone(payload.phone). Single source of truth: find_one filter (L365), update_one filter (L379), post-update read filter (L383), insert doc `phone` field (L388), and referral_code slicing at L373 & L409 all use canonical_phone. No drift between DB key and stored key.
Admin branch (L346-351) correctly short-circuits BEFORE normalize_indian_phone — canonical_phone = ADMIN_PHONE (raw 9999999999), preserving the pre-existing admin row and its /api/auth/me contract.
Bonus improvement: invalid phones like `12345`, `abcde`, `5xxxxxxxxx` now 400 in DEV verify-otp too (previously they only 400'd in prod via the MSG91 branch). Covers iter6 minor issue #4.

MSG91 helpers, IS_PROD gating, admin bypass, retry/backoff, and response contract {success,user,token} are unchanged from iter6 — no regression risk to the mocked prod-path tests (all 8 respx-based prod tests still green).
